date.note: IHEP dates the first BES physics paper, on the tau mass, to March 1992; the Phys. Rev. Lett. 69, 3021 paper is dated 23 November 1992 (APS), so the March 1992 date is likely the first report or preprint.

name: Measurement of the mass of the τ lepton
notes: The mass value in the key-value text is read from the TeX markup of the APS abstract; the tau mass fits the standard value used today but this record only reports what the abstract says.

summary.plain: BES, at the Beijing Electron-Positron Collider, measured the mass of the tau lepton by finding how the production of tau pairs turns on near threshold. IHEP says this precision measurement removed doubts about whether the tau behaves like the electron and muon.
summary.technical: BES: search near the e⁺e⁻ → τ⁺τ⁻ threshold, with one τ decaying to eνν̄ and the other to μνν̄; mass from a fit to the energy dependence of the cross section, m_τ = 1776.9 +0.4/−0.5 ± 0.2 MeV (Phys. Rev. Lett. 69, 3021, 1992).

title: Measurement of the mass of the τ lepton
why_it_matters: IHEP says the precision tau-mass measurement removed doubts about lepton universality.
